198np5jpkpc8rrnmun1jlgf8du: How many steps n takes to reach 1, after `taken`: halved (shifted down one bit) when even, 3n + 1 when odd (the Collatz map). Nobody has proved every n gets there; every n anyone has tried does.
2draobpjd6cs90vbunan182ahs: How many steps the numbers take to reach 1, all together: a fold adding each one's steps to the rest's. Each one's steps only compute, so on Node the compiled program works them out for runs of the numbers on worker threads and adds them up, the same sum as in turn (whole numbers add up the same in any order).
l1vp4c25ae7bdsmr0f9tq2lb2c: The numbers below `below` (the first argument, 300000 when there is none) whose way to 1 takes more than `longer than` steps (the second, 300): how many there are, the first few, the last, and the steps of all the numbers below together. They are kept with keep, whose test only computes, so on Node the compiled program tests runs of the numbers on worker threads, and the numbers kept are the same, in the same order, as testing them in turn.
program:
The numbers whose way to 1 under the Collatz map is long, kept by one keep (C43).
Prior art: the Collatz problem (Lothar Collatz, 1937); Lagarias, "The 3x + 1 problem and its generalizations" (1985).
